MOSAIC'S PHOTOGRAPHERS

Explore their fascinating lives, and view their copyright-free contributions to vintage and classic nude photography.

FELIX JACQUES MOULIN

March 26, 1802 – December 11, 1875

Born in Paris, France

Biography:
Félix-Jacques Moulin was a pivotal French photographer whose career reflects the dramatic tensions of 19th-century photography. Initially a controversial figure due to his provocative nude portraiture and resulting legal troubles, Moulin eventually transformed into a state-sponsored documentarian. His seminal three-volume series, L'Algérie photographiée, remains a landmark in Orientalist photography and colonial documentation, marking his transition from an artistic provocateur to a significant historical chronicler.

Prints & books

  • Global Gallery Budget GCS-455086-30-142 — Felix Jacques Moulin Female Nude (1856) Gallery Wrap Giclee on Canvas Print Wall Art. Affordable gallery-wrap canvas reproductions and framed options.

ANNE BRIGMAN

December 2, 1869 – February 7, 1950

Born in Honolulu, Hawaii, USA

Biography:
Anne Brigman was a central figure in the Photo-Secession movement and a pioneering West Coast photographer. She is best known for her expressive, allegorical images that depicted women in deep, mystical communion with the raw landscapes of the American West. Her work remains a foundational citation for the history of women reclaiming the landscape as a space for self-expression and environmental connection.

Prints & books

  • Anne Brigman: The Photographer of Enchantment — Hardcover (June 23, 2020) by Kathleen Pyne. A comprehensive study of Brigman's life and work, tracing her feminist, pictorialist vision and its influence on modern photography.

  • Anne Brigman: A Visionary in Modern Photography — Hardcover (Apr 22, 2020). Catalogue of the major retrospective exploring Brigman's pioneering role as a feminist and pictorialist photographer.

  • Anne Brigman's Songs: Her Life, Her Photographs, Her Poems — Hardcover (Nov 15, 2025) by James L. Rhem. A biographical and photographic study tracing Brigman's life, creative practice, and writings.

FRED HOLLAND DAY

July 22, 1864 – November 22, 1933

Born in Boston, Massachusetts, USA

Biography:
Fred Holland Day was a visionary American photographer, publisher, and intellectual who stood at the forefront of the Pictorialist movement. Known for his bold approach to fine art, he famously used the camera to explore sacred themes, mythology, and the male nude with a level of symbolism and intimacy that challenged the Victorian moral codes of his era. As both an artist and a publisher, he was instrumental in creating the intellectual framework that established photography as a legitimate, expressive art form.

Prints & books

  • Through an Uncommon Lens: The Life and Photography of F. Holland Day — Hardcover (Oct 15, 2008). Biography and retrospective covering Day's life, publishing work, and influence on pictorial photography; richly illustrated.

EUGENE DURIEU

December 9, 1800 – May 15, 1874

Born in Nîmes, France​

Biography:
Eugène Durieu was a pioneering French photographer and intellectual who played a pivotal role in the institutionalization of photography as an academic discipline. He is most renowned for his groundbreaking collaboration with painter Eugène Delacroix, providing anatomical nude studies that bridged the divide between traditional fine art painting and the emerging medium of photographic documentation.

Prints & books

  • Photographies d'apres des modeles poses 1854 — French edition (reprint 2017). Leather-bound reprint of the 1854 edition; high-quality reproduction, resized and processed for readability.

JANE DE LA VAUDÈRE

April 14, 1857 – July 25, 1908

Born in Paris, France

Biography:
Jane de La Vaudère was a formidable figure in the French Decadent movement, best known as a writer, poet, and avant-garde provocateur. Her creative output frequently intersected with the visual arts, as her rebellious themes and lush, symbolic prose provided a "visual blueprint" for the photographers and artists of fin-de-siècle Paris.

Prints & books

  • Resurrecting Jane de La Vaudère: Literary Shapeshifter of the Belle Époque — Paperback (Aug 27, 2024). Sharon Larson's study recovering the life, persona, and literary influence of Jane de La Vaudère, with biography and critical analysis.

  • The Demi-Sexes and The Androgynes — Paperback (June 12, 2018). Two novels by Jane de La Vaudère presented in English for the first time in Brian Stableford's translation; provocative fin-de-siècle fiction exploring transgressive themes.

  • Syta's Harem and Pharaoh's Lover — Paperback (June 30, 2020). Two exotic and decadent tales by Jane de La Vaudère, translated by Brian Stableford; richly atmospheric and provocative narratives.

ROBERT DEMACHY

July 6, 1859 – December 28, 1936

Born in Saint-Germain-en-Laye, France​

Biography:
Robert Demachy was a pioneering French photographer and the leading theorist of the Pictorialist movement in Europe. He is renowned for his mastery of the gum bichromate process, which allowed him to treat the photograph as a painterly canvas. By championing hand-manipulated, impressionistic images, Demachy waged a lifelong intellectual battle to establish photography as a subjective, interpretive art form rather than a purely mechanical reproduction of reality.

Prints & books

  • Robert Demachy 1859-1936: Photographs and Essays — Hardcover (1974). First American edition with ~95 pages and ~50 black-and-white photographs; an essential monograph for collectors and historians.

  • Robert Demachy: Impressions de Normandie — Paperback (June 17, 2016, French edition). A study of Demachy's work in Normandy and his leadership in the French pictorialist movement; richly illustrated and historically valuable.

CLARENCE HUDSON WHITE

April 7, 1871 – July 7, 1925

Born in West Carlisle, Ohio, USA

Biography:
Clarence Hudson White was a seminal American photographer and influential educator, best known as a founding member of the Photo-Secession movement. His work is celebrated for its poetic sensitivity, soft-focus aesthetic, and profound exploration of domesticity and light, while his pioneering school established the academic foundations for fine art photography in the United States.

Prints & books

  • Clarence H. White and His World: The Art and Craft of Photography, 1895–1925 — Restoring a gifted art photographer to his place in the American canon and, in the process, reshaping and expanding our understanding of early 20th-century American photography. Clarence H. White (1871–1925) was one of the most influential art photographers and teachers of the early 20th century and a founding member of the Photo-Secession. This beautiful publication offers a new appraisal of White’s contributions, including his groundbreaking aesthetic experiments, his commitment to the ideals of American socialism, and his embrace of the expanding fields of photographic book and fashion illustration, celebrity portraiture, and advertising. Based on extensive archival research, the book challenges the idea of an abrupt rupture between prewar, soft-focus idealizing.

  • Pictorial Photography in America 1920 — Kindle Edition. This edition was converted from its physical edition to digital by a community of volunteers; purchase of the Kindle edition includes wireless delivery.

MATTHEW BRADY

May 17, 1822 – January 14, 1896

Born in Warren County, New York, USA

Biography:
Mathew Brady is widely recognized as the "Father of Photojournalism." His work during the 19th century fundamentally changed the role of the camera, shifting it from a tool for portraiture to an instrument of historical truth and public consciousness. By documenting the American Civil War on a massive scale, he established the concept of the photographic archive, ensuring the camera would forever be regarded as an objective witness to human history.

ALFRED STIEGLITZ

December 31, 1863 – July 12, 1946

Born in Hoboken, New Jersey, USA

Biography:
Alfred Stieglitz was a foundational American photographer and modern art promoter who was instrumental in transforming photography from a technical craft into a globally recognized fine art form. As the editor of Camera Work and the founder of the legendary '291' gallery, he bridged the gap between the European Avant-Garde and the American art scene, leaving a legacy that fundamentally shaped 20th-century Modernism.

Prints & books

  • Discover Alfred Stieglitz's groundbreaking Camera Work - a beautifully curated multilingual hardcover collecting iconic photographs and essays. Explore images that shaped modern photography and own a timeless collector's edition.

  • Own the definitive two-volume Key Set - an elegant boxed collection showcasing Stieglitz's most powerful photographs. Perfect for collectors and photography lovers seeking a comprehensive museum-quality set.

  • Experience New York through Stieglitz's lens - a captivating volume of iconic urban photographs that capture mood, light and history. A must-have for anyone inspired by photography and the spirit of the city.

JULIA MARGARET CAMERON

June 10, 1815 – January 25, 1879

Born in Calcutta, India

Biography:
Julia Margaret Cameron was a pioneering British photographer and a central figure in the movement to establish photography as an expressive, fine art form. Known for her radical use of "soft focus" and long exposures, she captured evocative, emotionally charged portraits of 19th-century intellectuals and symbolic tableaux inspired by mythology and the Pre-Raphaelite movement. Her work remains a definitive study in the power of psychological portraiture.

EDWARD WESTON

March 23, 1886 – January 1, 1958

Born in Highland Park, Illinois, USA

Biography:
Edward Weston was a towering figure in 20th-century photography and a primary architect of Modernist photography. Known for his commitment to "Straight Photography," Weston rejected soft-focus styles in favor of extreme sharpness, deep clarity, and precise composition. As a founding member of Group f/64, he transformed organic objects, landscapes, and the human form into iconic, abstract sculptures, leaving an indelible mark on the history of fine art.

Prints & books

  • Edward Weston: The Flame of Recognition — Sixtieth Anniversary Edition (Paperback, July 1, 2025). A classic monograph bringing together images and excerpts from Weston's writing that present his feeling for life with photographic beauty.

  • Edward Weston: The Early Years — Hardcover (June 19, 2018). Explores Weston's early, painterly experiments and development prior to his mature modernist work; essential for understanding his artistic evolution.

MARIO VON BUCOVICH

May 27, 1884 – November 29, 1947

Born in Berlin, Germany

Biography:
Mario von Bucovich was a pioneering photographer celebrated for his dynamic urban cityscapes and his ability to capture the "spirit" of the world’s major metropolises. His work serves as a vital bridge between the aestheticized imagery of the late 19th century and the Modernist documentary realism that defined the interwar period in Berlin, Paris, and New York.

Prints & books

  • Berlin 1928: Das Gesicht der Stadt — German edition (Paperback, 1992) by Mario von Bucovich. A photographic portrait of Berlin in 1928 capturing the city's urban character and historical atmosphere; valuable for historians and collectors of early 20th-century photography.

  • Paris. Das Gesicht der Stadte — Hardcover (First German edition, 1928) by Mario v. Bucovich; essay by Paul Morand. Landmark visual study of Paris with historic photographs and contextual essays; a key volume for enthusiasts of interwar urban photography.

BARON WILHELM VON GLOEDEN

September 15, 1856 – February 15, 1931

Born in Wismar, Grand Duchy of Mecklenburg-Schwerin, Germany

Biography:
Baron Wilhelm von Gloeden was a German photographer celebrated for his evocative work in Taormina, Sicily. He is best known for his unique ability to fuse Classical Mediterranean themes with pictorialist photography, creating an artistic legacy that remains both highly influential and historically debated. His mastery of light and composition helped redefine the aesthetic possibilities of the nude study in the late 19th century.

Prints & books

  • Photographs of the Classic Male Nude — hardcover compilation (1977) featuring historic studio works and scholarly notes; excellent for collectors.

  • Von Gloeden et le XIXe siècle (Collection Nu masculin) — French edition exploring transnational 19th-century photography and artists; a valuable reference.

WILHELM VON PLUESCHOW

August 17, 1852 – January 2, 1930

Born in Wismar, Germany

Biography:
Wilhelm von Plüschow was a prominent German photographer known for his sophisticated studio-based nude photography. Operating primarily in Italy under the name "Guglielmo," his work stands as a cornerstone of late 19th-century aestheticism, blending classical art references with an intimate, psychologically direct portraiture style that remains a complex case study in the history of art and censorship.

Prints & books

  • Galdi / Gloeden / Pluschow: Sammlung Uwe Scheid Aktaufnahmen (Bibliothek des Blicks, Band 3) — Hardcover (1993). German edition edited by Uwe Scheid; features photography by Vincenzo Galdi and Wilhelm von Gloeden; high-quality reprint for collectors.

  • Gloeden, Pluschow, Galdi — Hardcover (Spanish edition). Collection showcasing work by Wilhelm von Gloeden, Guglielmo Plüschow and Vincenzo Galdi; richly illustrated volume for photography enthusiasts.

  • Wilhelm von Gloeden, von Plüschow, Galdi — Sicilien Beautés / Sicilian Beauties (French-English edition) — Hardcover (2014). Bilingual illustrated volume featuring classic Sicilian studio portraits and historical commentary.
